title: Needs or Wants?
source_body:
Needs or Wants?

Every day, we spend money on many different things. But have you ever stopped to ask yourself whether you really need what you are buying?

Economists divide the things we buy into two groups: needs and wants. Needs are things that we must have to live, such as food, clothes, and a place to stay. Wants are things that make life more fun or comfortable but are not necessary, such as new games, designer shoes, or the latest phone.

It is not wrong to buy things we want. The problem is that our money is limited, but our wants are not. Advertisements and social media make us feel that we always need something new. If we spend too much money on wants, we may not have enough for our needs or for the future.

That is why making a budget is important. A budget is a plan that shows how much money you will spend and save. One helpful tip is the "24-hour rule." When you want to buy something that is not a need, wait for 24 hours before buying it. Often, you will find that you don't really want it anymore.

Managing money wisely is a skill that will help you for the rest of your life.

variants.prestudy:
Needs or Wants?

On a daily basis, we spend money on an astonishing array of goods and services. Yet have you ever paused to consider whether you genuinely require what you are purchasing?

Economists categorize our purchases into two fundamental groups: needs and wants. Needs are items indispensable to survival, such as food, clothing, and shelter. Wants, by contrast, are items that enhance our enjoyment or comfort but are by no means essential, such as new video games, designer footwear, or the latest smartphone.

Purchasing things we desire is not inherently wrong. The difficulty lies in the fact that whereas our financial resources are finite, our wants are virtually limitless. Advertisements and social media relentlessly create the impression that we are perpetually in need of something new. Should we spend excessively on wants, we may be left with insufficient funds for our needs or for the future.

It is for this reason that establishing a budget is crucial. A budget is a financial plan that specifies how much money you intend to spend and how much you aim to save. One practical strategy is the so-called "24-hour rule." Whenever you are tempted to buy something that is not a necessity, postpone the purchase for 24 hours. More often than not, you will find that your desire for it has faded.

Managing money prudently is a skill that will serve you well throughout your life.
